question: GQ-007
subject: 777 books, and the scans that made every gate slow

the_fifth_list_is_complete.across_five_lists: every failure transient — not one book permanently unavailable

the_scans.where_they_ran: search --stats, build-library-page, build-observatory, AND three declared derivations the audit re-runs on every gate invocation
the_scans.effect: npm run verify exceeded ten minutes; search --stats took 506s

fix: the builders persist corpus_stats and modern_stats; every consumer reads them
the_general_lesson: the fix for a slow query is an index-shaped query or a stored aggregate — never a smaller batch. Third time this session.

two_crashes_and_a_recovery.first: modern index died at 940,000 of 981,260 — offset paging degraded 6ms at offset 1,000 to 27,273ms at offset 900,000, a 4,500x fall
two_crashes_and_a_recovery.fix: bounded at 200k entries, plus --resume so a crash does not restart an hour of work
two_crashes_and_a_recovery.second: died again near the end — an UNBOUNDED word cache keyed on every f-containing word across 88.6M words, where OCR garbage supplies unlimited variety
two_crashes_and_a_recovery.recovery: a 5.6 MB rollback journal blocked read-only opens; opening writable let sqlite replay it — 454,000 rows preserved, no data loss

a_guard_that_checked_the_wrong_thing.what: the pipeline verified passage_modern EXISTS, not that it is complete
a_guard_that_checked_the_wrong_thing.consequence: reported success with 334,000 of 981,260 rows, and long_s_passages would have been published as 53,517 — a count that FELL while the corpus grew
a_guard_that_checked_the_wrong_thing.fix: the pipeline now compares row counts and exits 1 on a mismatch
